name: Nebraska

fees.note: 408 NAC 3-009.04: single trip overdimensional only $15; OD+OW combined permit $25 total. Valid up to 10 moving days.
408 NAC 3-009.04: combined overdimensional + overweight single trip $25.

escorts.when: Over 11'11" wide, on interstates and freeways
Over 11'11" wide, on two-lane and other roads
Over 124'11" long, on interstates and freeways
Over 124'11" long, on two-lane and other roads

restrictions.text: Overdimensional moves: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset only; no travel on designated holidays/long holidays (typically from noon the day before until sunrise after; dates on NDOT holiday schedule and on the permit).
No overdimensional travel Mon-Fri 7:00-9:00 am and 4:00-6:00 pm in Lincoln (US-6/34/77, N-2 inside city limits) and the Omaha urban area, incl. I-80 from Iowa line to MP 432 (Gretna).
Overdimensional travel prohibited in rain, sleet, snow, slippery surfaces, visibility under 1/2 mile, or hazardous wind.
Overweight-only permits are valid 24 hours/day, 7 days/week, including holidays and regardless of weather.

travel.holidays: No travel from noon the day before through the holiday; a Monday or Friday holiday closes the long weekend

sources.title: 408 NAC Chapter 3 - Permits for Movement of Overweight and/or Overdimensional Vehicles and Loads
NDOT - Legal Sizes and Weights for Vehicles in Nebraska

notes: Escorts 'may be required' at the Department's discretion for any load over 8'6" wide, 90' long or 14'6" high (408 NAC 3-003.19A); the escort rules here model only the mandatory thresholds.

On State freeways/expressways/rural divided highways (incl. I-80) the rear escort may be omitted if the trailer has rear-facing amber flashing/strobe lights visible at 800 ft (003.19E); this calculator still counts the rear escort on interstate.
Superloads need Lincoln Permit Office (and possibly Bridge Division/District) review; allow 5-10 business days.
Legal gross is 80,000 lb on Interstate and up to 94,000 lb on US/State routes subject to the Nebraska axle/bridge table; calculator uses 80,000.
Pole car 'may be required' for loads over 14'6" high; mandatory at 16' and higher.
